overview: A stubborn low off the coast brings rain and mountain snow to the Pacific Northwest, then a string of wet frontal systems takes over the week. Wet weather favors the Coast Mountains and Cascades, while the northern Rockies stay drier until a stronger system arrives around Thanksgiving.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Rain is the main story here, with snow mostly confined to higher ground. Warm air keeps the snow level high, so the mountains see rain until a cooler spell by midweek. Whistler's best snow falls Tuesday and Wednesday, when wet snow and rain mix at the top. Expect heavy, wet snow rather than powder at mid-mountain elevations.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A series of Pacific systems pushes through with widespread precipitation and gusty southeast winds. Snow levels rise Monday and Tuesday, so the higher passes such as Stevens get the snow while lower slopes get rain. The Cascade snowpack picks up most heavily Wednesday, when cold air returns behind the front, and Mt. Baker and Crystal Mountain see the best of it. Wind chill and gusts near 40 mph make the upper mountain cold and rough.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Monday brings only a passing chance of light snow showers in western Wyoming. Tuesday and Wednesday turn drier as a ridge builds, with breezy conditions across Montana. The pattern turns more active from Thanksgiving onward, with snow showers at Jackson Hole and Grand Targhee and stronger winds aloft through Friday. Big Sky sees only light amounts.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Light flurries and mixed precipitation are the main weather here this week. Snow levels stay low, so Thursday brings a mix of snow and rain. Friday and Friday night turn to steady rain, which will limit the snowfall at Revelstoke and Whitewater. Temperatures stay near freezing, so expect wet snow at best.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
